items.q: Which is cheaper, GoHighLevel or Systeme.io?
items.a: Systeme.io is cheaper at every published tier. Its Free plan costs $0 a month forever, covering 2,000 contacts, 3 sales funnels and 1 course with no credit card required, and its paid tiers run $17 (Startup), $47 (Webinar) and $97 (Unlimited) a month. GoHighLevel has no free plan; its cheapest tier, Starter, costs $97 a month before any usage, matching Systeme.io's top Unlimited plan. That $97 buys unlimited users and contacts plus a CRM, funnel builder and phone system, but texting, calling, email and most AI are billed separately from a prepaid wallet, so a small team's real GoHighLevel bill runs closer to $125.42 a month once typical usage is added. Systeme.io charges 0% on every sale and meters nothing beyond the plan price. For a business that will not use a phone system or CRM sub-accounts, Systeme.io is cheaper at every size; GoHighLevel's cost only makes sense once those features are actually in use.

items.q: Does Systeme.io have a CRM like GoHighLevel's?
items.a: Systeme.io includes CRM pipelines, up to 100 of them on its Unlimited plan, so it is not just an email list. What it does not include is a phone and texting system: GoHighLevel builds local and toll-free numbers, calls and SMS into every plan, billed per use from a prepaid wallet, while Systeme.io's help centre says SMS sending goes through your own connected Twilio account at Twilio's rates instead. GoHighLevel is built around its CRM and phone system first, with unlimited contacts and users on every plan, including the $97 Starter tier. Systeme.io's CRM sits alongside funnels, courses and email as one of several features rather than the centerpiece, and its Free and Startup plans cap contacts at 2,000 and 5,000. A business that wants pipeline stages paired with native calling and texting gets that from GoHighLevel; one that wants simple deal tracking bundled with a funnel and course platform gets that from Systeme.io instead.

items.q: Which one is better for a marketing agency with multiple clients?
items.a: GoHighLevel, for most agencies. Its Starter plan includes 3 sub-accounts for $97 a month, and Unlimited at $297 a month removes that cap and lets an agency rebill phone and email usage to clients at cost; Agency Pro at $497 a month adds marked-up rebilling and a full SaaS-resale mode. Systeme.io also allows unlimited sub-accounts on every plan, including Free, but each one simply shares the main account's plan limits rather than supporting rebilled usage, and Systeme.io's own pricing FAQ and help centre disagree on how its separate white-label pricing works. GoHighLevel also bundles the phone and texting system a local-service or appointment-based client typically needs for follow-up, which Systeme.io does not build in. An agency whose clients mainly need more funnels and courses, with no calling or rebilling, can still run each client's work from a Systeme.io sub-account instead.

items.q: Can Systeme.io send text messages the way GoHighLevel does?
items.a: Not natively. GoHighLevel builds SMS into every plan, including the $97 Starter tier, and bills it by the segment, close to $0.0075 each, plus a small carrier fee, once a one-time $22.50 A2P 10DLC registration is done. Systeme.io has no SMS pricing or sending system of its own; its help centre says texting works only by connecting your own Twilio account, and Twilio bills those messages separately at Twilio's own rates, outside your Systeme.io subscription entirely. That means the per-message cost on Systeme.io depends on your Twilio plan and destination country, not on which Systeme.io tier you pay for. A business built around text follow-up, appointment reminders or lead nurturing by SMS gets that out of the box from GoHighLevel's first dollar; the same business would need to set up and fund a separate Twilio account before Systeme.io could send a single text.

items.q: Which one should a course creator or coach choose?
items.a: Systeme.io is the closer fit for most course creators and coaches. Its Free plan already includes 1 course with up to 500 students, 3 sales funnels and unlimited email sends at $0 a month, and paid tiers starting at $17 add more funnels and courses, with evergreen webinars arriving on the $47 Webinar plan, all without ever taking a cut of a sale. GoHighLevel also includes courses and communities, but they sit alongside a full CRM, calendars and a phone and texting system a course creator typically will not touch, and its $97 Starter plan still requires A2P texting registration before sending a single SMS reminder. The exception is a coach also running an agency-style business with multiple client accounts or heavy calling for enrollment follow-up; that workflow leans back toward GoHighLevel's CRM and sub-account structure. For a course creator focused on selling and delivering one course through funnels and email, Systeme.io's lower floor and course-first bundling fit better.

items.q: How hard is it to switch between GoHighLevel and Systeme.io?
items.a: Switching cost depends mostly on timing, not a shared export tool between the two. Systeme.io offers a free done-for-you migration service to anyone on its Unlimited plan or any annual plan, something GoHighLevel does not match with an equivalent service of its own. Moving off GoHighLevel is the more time-sensitive direction: every plan cancels from the dashboard whenever you want, but any balance left in its prepaid usage wallet is forfeited 30 days after cancellation unless you request a refund first, and a canceled account's data is deleted after 90 days. Moving off Systeme.io is gentler on the account side, since cancellation takes effect just before your next renewal rather than immediately, but its subscriptions are non-refundable and downgrading to a lower tier needs a support ticket and a custom order form rather than a self-serve setting. Moving toward GoHighLevel, ask about Systeme.io's migration help first; moving toward Systeme.io, time your GoHighLevel cancellation around the wallet, not the calendar.
